candidates.review_note: A candidate has a chance iff allocating all remaining votes to that candidate places it among the top k positive-vote candidates, using the actual last-vote tie breaker. To test certainty, leave its current positive count unchanged and compute the minimum additional votes each rival needs to outrank it. Rivals already ahead cost0; every other rival receiving new votes must exceed its count because a new tied last vote is later. If the k cheapest rival costs fit the remaining budget, exclusion is possible. Zero-vote candidates are never treated as guaranteed merely because empty seats exist.

Dynamic programming over consumed digits keeps every attainable prefix gcd, with a bitset of attainable segment counts for that gcd. Append each next segment of at most M digits, updating gcd and shifting the count bitset. Prune only counts that cannot meet the final separator bounds even with minimum/maximum remaining segment lengths. Leading zeroes and gcd(0,0)=0 are handled by ordinary integer accumulation. Keeping all gcd states avoids the invalid greedy assumption that the largest intermediate gcd always leads to the best final result.
